answer: Because the fable cluster is derived from funding history, the split is applied at settlement and the grove audit lists each share. That makes each additional alias in a cluster strictly dilutive, so the operator pays the bond and the lotus fee for a smaller payout than one honest position would earn. The reward pool is divided per detected cluster rather than per key, so 172 linked identities split one share instead of collecting 172 of them. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
